title: Edges of the rule
description: The ferry charges by age. Test right at the edges of each price, where off-by-one bugs hide.

tasks.title: Bugs live at the edges
tasks.body: A rule like "children from 5 to 12 pay 5" has edges: 4 and 5, then 12 and 13. Off-by-one bugs, such as < where <= was meant, change the answer only right at an edge.
tasks.detail: For every edge, test the value on each side of it. Testing 8 and 30 says little about whether 12 counts as a child. 0 and 1, an empty list and a one-item list, and the first and last positions are edges too.

tasks.code:
def can_ride(height):
    return height >= 120

assert can_ride(119) == False
assert can_ride(120) == True
assert can_ride(121) == True
print("both sides of 120 tested")
tasks.note: 119 and 120 sit either side of the edge, and 121 is just past it. A bug in >= would show up in one of the first two.

tasks.question: If can_ride() said height > 120, which assert would fail?
tasks.why: Only exactly 120 is treated differently by > and >=, so only the test right on the edge notices.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: change >= to > and check. Then add a second rule, height <= 200, and test both sides of 200.

The ferry has a function ticket_price(age) in the check:

- under 5 travel free
- ages 5 to 12 pay 5
- ages 13 to 64 pay 10
- 65 and over pay 6

Write asserts that test it, especially at the edges. The check runs your tests on the correct ticket_price(), where they must all pass, and on broken versions, where at least one must fail for each. Do not write ticket_price() yourself.
hints: List the edges first: where does each price start and stop? Each edge needs a test on both sides of it.
The rule has three edges, at 5, at 13 and at 65. A test on the last age of one price and the first age of the next catches a bug at that edge.
With other names: for a rule that 120 and over may ride, assert can_ride(119) == False and assert can_ride(120) == True test both sides of its edge.

error_hints.text: A test failed on the correct ticket_price(). Read the rule again: from 5 to 12 includes both 5 and 12.
ticket_price() takes one whole number, the age.
The check provides ticket_price(): spell it exactly that way.
Your tests passed on a ticket_price() that lets 5-year-olds travel free. Test age 5.
Your tests passed on a ticket_price() that charges 12-year-olds the full price. Test age 12.
Your tests passed on a ticket_price() with a broken edge. Test the ages on both sides of every edge.
Your tests passed on a ticket_price() with a broken edge. Check the edge between children and the full price from both sides.

assert can_ride(119) == False

similar_example.note: One edge, tested on both sides. Your ticket rule has three edges.

other_ways.note: A dictionary of edge ages and their prices, checked in a loop.
Testing every age from 0 to 99 against the rule written out again. Thorough, but if you copy the same bug into both, the test cannot see it.
